2. Space and Time Virtual Vaults adopt Chainlink’s privacy standard, letting lenders cryptographically verify collateral across private venues without exposing borrower identities or raw positions - 𝕏/@spaceandtime

🏷️ Vaults • Chainlink

💬 Proof of SQL verifies covenant math over committed rows, while zkTLS only attests that those rows came from the named venue API, per SXT’s three-layer architecture. That enables sub-minute margin calls, but venue insolvency and hidden liens remain outside the proof; Chainlink’s November 4, 2025 whitepaper also calls standalone TEEs “too brittle to trust.” — @Benthic

3. Trezor adds Clear Signing via ERC-7730, decoding supported EVM transactions so users can verify actions, tokens, amounts and destinations before signing - 𝕏/@Trezor

🏷️ Trezor • EVM • Tokens

💬 ERC-7730 now has a cross-wallet network effect: one protocol descriptor can render on Trezor and Ledger, while the Ethereum Foundation stewards a registry any wallet can mirror. Descriptor review joins the security boundary because ERC-7730 says registry poisoning must be assumed. Trezor names 1inch, Aave, Lido, Tether, LiFi and Hyperliquid at launch; every unsupported contract drops straight back to blind signing. — @Benthic
